title: Release-record, tag, and readiness gates hold on committed history
setupCommands:
git init -b main -q && git add -A && git commit -S -qm "chore: initial import" && git tag v1.0.0 && mkdir -p .changeset && printf -- '---
"@acme/api": patch
---

Retry now doubles its backoff.
' > .changeset/fix-retry-backoff.md && monochange prepare >/dev/null 2>&1 && monochange step commit-release >/dev/null 2>&1 && monochange step tag-release --from HEAD --push=false >/dev/null 2>&1
expectation: After a release has been prepared and committed, three gates hold. monochange step release-record --from <tag> resolves the durable .monochange/releases/<id>/release.json file from the tagged commit's first-parent history. monochange step tag-release refuses an import ref with no release record and requires its target commit itself to be the release commit before creating a tag. monochange step publish-readiness reads the committed record without publishing; the fixture's unpublished npm package reports blocked and names its bootstrap remedy.

checks.why: The tagged history must contain a committed release.json carrying the released version; publish-readiness and tag-release resolve this durable record rather than an embedded commit-body snapshot.

checks.command: sha=$(monochange step release-record --sha --from v1.0.1 2>/dev/null | tail -1); echo "$sha" | grep -qE '^[0-9a-f]{40}$'
checks.why: The step must resolve a real commit for the tag, not just report the record kind.

checks.command: monochange step tag-release --from v1.0.0 --push=false > .gate.out 2>&1; rc=$?; grep -q 'no monochange release record found in first-parent ancestry' .gate.out; found=$?; rm -f .gate.out; test $rc -eq 1 -a $found -eq 0
checks.why: The target commit itself must be a release-record commit. The fixture's import tag has no release record and must be refused.

checks.command: git tag -d v1.0.1 >/dev/null 2>&1; monochange step tag-release --from HEAD --push=false > .gate.out 2>&1; rc=$?; git rev-parse -q --verify refs/tags/v1.0.1 >/dev/null; tagged=$?; rm -f .gate.out; test $rc -eq 0 -a $tagged -eq 0
checks.why: On a genuine release commit the step must create the tag locally. The tag is deleted first and left in place afterwards so the readiness check below still sees it.

checks.command: monochange step publish-readiness --from v1.0.1 --format json > .ready.out 2>&1; rc=$?; grep -q '"status": "blocked"' .ready.out; a=$?; grep -q 'monochange step placeholder-publish' .ready.out; b=$?; rm -f .ready.out; test $rc -eq 0 -a $a -eq 0 -a $b -eq 0
checks.why: Readiness must run to completion without touching a registry, and for a package that has never published it must say `blocked` and name the bootstrap remedy rather than claiming readiness.
